en: And what's also important to understand when
working with Codex or similar tools is that
you're working on a limited context window.
All your prompts and all the code that's
analyzed by Codex and all the code that's
generated and also tool calls, so the
internal instructions it processes and a
bunch of other stuff, all of that goes into
a limited context window. And the size of
that window depends on the model. You're
using, and of course,
newer models will likely have a bigger
context window, but it will be limited. Now,
if you exceed that context window,
if you got some instructions or some code
that's loaded that goes outside of the
available context window size,
Codex will automatically compact that
window,
which means it will create a summary of the
context that was inside of it and then
continue with that summary, which of course
means some context will get lost. It's
summarized after all. And actually it will
technically start that compaction process
before it reaches the limit, of course,
because once it reaches it,
well, it couldn't continue. Now this
compaction can also be triggered manually
with
/compact. So if you know that your context
window is already pretty full
and you can tell by this indication,
obviously this one here is pretty much
empty.
But if you knew that it were pretty full and
that you had a bigger task coming up, which
for some reason you don't wanna run in a new
session, you could run compact to have it
generate that summary. And then it would
free up the majority of the context window
and just load that summary into it.
So here you see, of course, the summary here
is so short that we now got the full context
window available again.
Now, as mentioned, it will do that
compaction automatically if it runs out of
space,
but in most cases, you wanna try avoid
hitting those limits. And therefore,
typically, if you start working on a new
task, you wanna start a new session, either
by opening a new terminal window and running
Codex in there, in your project folder, of
course,
or
by running
/new.
This has the same effect. It clears the
context window and starts a new session.
In the IDE integration, as mentioned, it's
this New Chat button.
And in the Codex app, it's this New Thread
button here.
Auto-compaction works here in the desktop
app and in the IDE integration too though.
So it does that for you, but you typically
wanna avoid it because context is king, as
you will also learn throughout this course.
